text:
sophia: Quick bring-up summary for pyxis9b-int4 — ran the initial eval sweep (chat + MRR Q/A) and a small perf pass. Posting high-level numbers, then recs.

sophia: Metrics (batch=1, seq=512, single-GPU):
```
- fp16 baseline MRR: 0.672
- int4 MRR: 0.647  (delta: -0.025 => -3.7%)
- fp16 p95 latency: 140ms
- int4 p95 latency: 118ms
- tokens/sec (fp16): 420
- tokens/sec (int4): 730
- estimated token unit cost diff: ~0.45x (int4 vs fp16)
```

sophia: Observations: int4 yields strong throughput and ~2.2x speedups at token level, unit cost looks attractive for high-volume features. But MRR drop ~3.7% is noticeable on hard Q/A slices. Short chit-chat and short prompt completion look indistinguishable.

marco: Do we have breakdown by prompt length & temperature? my gut: long-context generative tasks might see larger quality regressions.

sophia: We ran short/long split: long (>1024) sample size small, but delta increased to ~6% on our long-QA subset; mostly hallucination-ish failures. Temp=0.0 used for MRR evals.

alin: Thanks. My read: safe to route low-risk, high-throughput routes (embeds + quick assistant replies <256 tokens) to int4. For electable/critical paths (ranks/paid features, long-context summarization) keep fp16 or int6.

zoe: From GTN/product POV — what's the recommended rollout tactic? We want to avoid regressing paid customers.

alin: Proposal: multilane routing + canary:
- Default PLG tier -> pyxis9b-int4 for <=256 tokens, 99th percentile quality monitored on our eval hooks.
- Paid tier -> fallback to int6/fp16 for >256 or flagged prompts.
- Canary: 1% traffic with golden prompts (existing scorecard) for 48h, auto-rollback on MRR drop >1.5% on golden set.

marco: Agree. Also suggest prompt-preserve trick (prefix calibration) — we saw ~0.8% MRR gain on int4 by adding a short calibration prompt and re-ranking top-k logits. Cheap and worth A/B.

sophia: Noted. Action items:
- sophia: run 48h canary with golden-set + calibrator enabled (start with k=5 re-rank).
- alin: implement routing flags (<=256 default to int4, else to int6).
- zoe: draft GTN/PD note for customer-facing guidance (rollback thresholds, expected cost delta).
- marco: run longer-context sweep and sanity-check hallucination taxonomy.

deploy-bot: Canary schedule created: pyxis9b-int4 canary -> start 2026-03-21T03:00Z, duration 48h, rollout 1%. See: https://deploys.redwood.internal/canary/2712345678

zoe: Perfect. One more ask: if canary passes, what % should we aim for as next step for PLG?

alin: If golden-set MRR change <0.5% and no latency/regression alerts, move to 20% for 24h, then 50% for 24h, monitor. Keep paid tier off int4 unless A/B proves parity.

sophia: Thanks — I'll post results summary after 48h and include per-slice breakdown (short vs long, hallucination types).

marco: :thumbsup:
